examples.name: Default
examples.summary: Default dropdown with a single unlabeled group of six options and no left/right affordances. Click the trigger to open; controls drive placement, offset, and disabled.

examples.name: Groups
examples.summary: Two labeled groups (`Account`, `Workspace`) separated by an automatic top divider on the second group. One option carries a `command` hint, another is `selected` — the central anatomy of this component.

examples.name: States
examples.summary: Panel forced open (`open="true"`) showing each spec-declared option state side-by-side: `default`, `selected`, and `disabled`. The `hover` and `focus-visible` states are interactive — focus an option with the keyboard (`Down` / `Up`) or hover with the pointer to see them.

examples.name: Placements
examples.summary: All four explicit `placement` values side-by-side. Click each trigger to see how the panel anchors against it. Panels are teleported to `body` and positioned with `position: fixed` against the trigger's bounding rect — no external positioning runtime.

examples.name: AutoPlacement
examples.summary: `placement="auto"` lets the dropdown choose the best-fitting corner at open time. The four triggers below all use the same prop value — each resolves to a different placement based on the available space around them. The resolved value is reflected in `data-placement` on the open panel.

examples.name: OptionAffordances
examples.summary: Panel forced open showing every option affordance: plain label, `command` keyboard hint, `left` icon slot, `right` content slot (with a `Tag`), `selected` state, and `disabled` state. The `command` prop and the `right` slot are mutually exclusive — pick one per option.

examples.name: WithTopAndBottomSlots
examples.summary: Root `top` and `bottom` named slots in use — typically a search input at the top and a footer action at the bottom. Both regions stick to their edges and stay outside the scrollable group list.

examples.name: GroupsWithTopAndBottomSlots
examples.summary: Two groups each using the `top` and `bottom` slots — a per-section caption above the options and a footer action below. Different from the root `top`/`bottom` (which are sticky outside the scroll area), group-level slots render inline within the section.

examples.name: CustomTriggers
examples.summary: `Dropdown.Trigger` is abstract — it wires `aria-haspopup`/`aria-expanded`/`aria-controls` and the open/close click onto whatever element you put inside its default slot. Here it wraps an `IconButton` (row actions) and an `Avatar` (account menu).
